rawFindings.title: Potential TypeError when accessing undefined bucket in List.files getter
rawFindings.explanation: The change removed the fallback to an empty array when accessing this.buckets.get(p.pattern) in the files getter. If the bucket for the pattern does not exist, this will cause from(undefined) which throws an error.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore fallback to empty array: return from(self.buckets.get(p.pattern) || []).sort(byPath)
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: If this.buckets lacks an entry for a pattern, accessing this.files will throw a TypeError due to calling from(undefined).

rawFindings.title: Throwing Promise.CancellationError loses original rejection error
rawFindings.explanation: In changeFile, if the stat.mtime is not newer, the code throws a new Promise.CancellationError, causing the original statAsync rejection to be lost. It may be more correct to reject with the CancellationError instead of throwing it synchronously.
rawFindings.suggestion: Replace `throw new Promise.CancellationError()` with `return Promise.reject(new Promise.CancellationError())`
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: If stat.mtime is not greater than file.mtime, the thrown CancellationError is unhandled as a synchronous throw in a Promise chain.
